en: The Dhāraṇī Named Grahamātṛkā;
the Noble Dhāraṇī Named Grahamātṛkā.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Mother of the Planets!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was in the great city of Aḍakavatī, being praised by many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, apasmāras, Āditya, Soma, Aṅgāra, Budha, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, Ketu, and others, as well as the twenty-eight lunar mansions and so forth; he was established in the empowerment of the array of the Great Vajra-Samaya Ornament.
He was dwelling upon the lion throne together with many thousands of bodhisattvas,
such as the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajrapāṇi.
and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajracaṇḍa; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajrasena;
and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajravināyaka.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajracāpahasta,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajravikurvita,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajrādhipati;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajrālaṃkāra;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vajravikrama;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Jyotirvajra.
And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara;
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samantabhadra;
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samantāvalokiteśvara.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Lokaśrī;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Padmaketu;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnaketu.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vikasitavaktra,
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Padmagarbha,
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Padmanetra.

The Blessed One was teaching the Dharma, surrounded and honored by hundreds of thousands of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, headed by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Maitreya.

He proclaimed the holy life that is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end; excellent in meaning and excellent in phrasing; unique, complete, pure, and utterly refined.
He taught the Dharma discourse named *The Great Array Ornament of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel*.
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having surveyed that circle of the assembly, rose from his seat and,

by means of his own supernatural power (*ṛddhyādhiṣṭhāna*), circumambulated the Blessed One hundreds of thousands of times. Having prostrated and sat down before him, he assumed a cross-legged posture with pride, and looking with playful grace at that circle of the assembly, [formed] the vajra-añjali.
Having established the Blessed One within his own heart, he said this:
"Blessed One, the planets—whether of fierce or non-fierce form, of violent or non-violent form, or of cruel or non-cruel form—torment sentient beings.
They take away the life-force of some, they cause calamities for some, they act as stealers of vitality for some, they seize the possessions of some, and [they afflict] those long-lived beings..."
They cause [beings] to have short lifespans;
thus they drive all sentient beings about with calamities.
Therefore, may the Blessed One teach this Dharma-discourse by which there will be protection for all sentient beings from all calamities.

The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! Since you, having generated a mind of compassion for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings, inquire of the Tathāgata, the perfectly enlightened one, regarding that which is most secret among secrets, listen to it; attend well and thoroughly, and I shall speak to you."

For the planets of fierce form, with cruel and most terrifying faces, there is a divine worship, an offering of water (argha), recitation, and incense—more secret than the most secret—that accords with their respective colors so that those planets may be satisfied.
When worshipped, they respond with worship; otherwise, they consume [the practitioner] from wherever he is brought. //1//
The gods and also the asuras, the kinnaras and the mahoragas, the yakṣas and the rākṣasas, as well as humans and non-humans. // 2 //
They pacify those who are angry and, being greatly compassionate, they act with splendor.
I shall now proclaim their worship and their mantras as well, in due order. (3)

Then indeed, the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Perfectly Awakened One, emitted from his own heart a flaming ray of light named *Karuṇāvikrīḍita* (Sport of Compassion) and caused it to enter the crowns of the planets.

At that very moment, all those planets, beginning with Āditya, arose and, having honored the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One with every divine offering, bowed down and fell upon their knees.
With palms joined in reverence, they said this to the Blessed One:

"We have been favored by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Therefore, may the Blessed One teach such a Dharma discourse by which we may [serve] a Dharma-preacher who has become a member of the assembly."

We shall provide protection; we shall effect guarding, rescue, acceptance, preservation, peace, well-being, avoidance of punishment, avoidance of weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth.
Then indeed, the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke the mantra-worship of the planets:
Oṃ megholkāya svāhā!
Oṃ śītāṃśave svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to Raktāṅgakumāra!
Oṃ, svāhā to Budha! Oṃ, svāhā to Bṛhaspati!
Oṃ, to the supreme asura, svāhā! Oṃ, to the one of black complexion, svāhā!
Oṃ, to Rāhu, svāhā!
Oṃ jyotiḥketave svāhā!

According to the sequence of the divisions, one should construct a fragrant maṇḍala in the center of a lotus: a square measuring twelve finger-breadths, with four gates and adorned with four archways, a gabled chamber (*kūṭāgāra*) equipped with a wheel, [representing] the cardinal and intermediate directions.

In the center of that, upon a white lotus and a maṇḍala of saffron-scented paste, one should contemplate the god Bhāskara, who assumes the form of an ascetic, holding a white lotus with both arms, red in color, and possessing a body garlanded with splendor equal to ten million thousand suns.
For him, milk-food and kunduru incense should be offered.

Oṃ megholkāya svāhā! In the eastern direction, upon a red lotus on a maṇḍala of priyaṅgu fragrance, one should know that Soma is a Brāhmaṇa; he is white in color, wears a crown of matted hair adorned with flowers, his food is ghee-rice, and his incense is śrīvāsa.
Oṃ candrāmṛtavikramāya namaḥ!
Svāhā to Śītāṃśu!

In the southern direction, upon a white lotus on a circular mandala of sandalwood fragrance, is Maṅgala in the form of a monk, red in color, wearing a jewel crown; he holds a spear in his left hand and has a hand in the gesture of granting boons in his right; his food is milk-rice or rice cooked with sesame; the incense is guggulu.
Oṃ, homage to the Youth blazing with red embers;
to Aṅgāra, svāhā!
In the western direction, upon a red lotus and a maṇḍala of black agallochum incense, there is the student Budha, yellow in color with a red beard, holding a rosary and a water-pot.
The food is mudga beans, rice, and split peas;
the incense is fragrant resin.
Oṃ, homage to the yellow-colored Prince.
Svāhā to Budha!

In the northern direction, upon a white lotus on a fragrant mandala of *devadāru* wood, is the wandering ascetic Guru, with the luster of molten gold and red beard, holding a rosary and a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*).
To him should be offered curd-rice, boiled rice, or milk, along with honey, ghee, and incense.
Oṃ, homage to the one of red complexion who has reached the Vedas; svāhā to the abode of enjoyment!

(Gmdh 174) In the southeastern direction, upon a red lotus and a maṇḍala of sandalwood fragrance, [is] the white Pāśupata holding a white [garment]; he is white as cow’s milk, bearing matted hair, a crown, a rosary, and a water-pot.
To him, a meal of milk and camphor incense should be offered.
*Oṃ namaḥ śukrādhipataye asurottamāya śuddhavigrahe svāhā*.

In the southwestern direction, upon a white lotus on a fragrant mandala of blue sandalwood, one should know Śanaiścara to be dark-complexioned, a mendicant with a hooded serpent, possessing a seed-syllable, matted locks, a crown, and a beard.
His lower lip is moist with the sap of the *kṣikṣirika* used for his rosary; his food consists of rice mixed with sesame;
his incense is fragrant resin (*gandharasa*).
Oṃ, homage to the one who resembles the color blue!
*Svāhā* to Kṛṣṇa-Śaniścara!

In the northwest direction, upon a red lotus on a circular mandala of fragrances such as tagara, is Rāhu, the Kāpālika; he resembles a sapphire (*rājāvarta*), has a body that is half [of his usual form], possesses a pair of eyes as terrifying as the chariot of the Sun, is formidable with fangs, and has five colors on his forehead marked by a frown.
Standing amidst clouds with his two arms positioned in the gestures of the moon, the sun, and the lotus;
for him, one should offer food consisting of meat or a porridge of sesame, and incense made from *vilva* leaves.
OṂ, homage to Rāhu, the one with a distorted face, the consumer of blood, who resembles bumblebees and collyrium!
Svāhā to Amṛtapriya!
In the northeastern direction, upon a red lotus and a mandala of spṛkkā fragrance, there shall be Cāṇḍālaketu;
he is smoke-colored, with palms joined in reverence, having the form of a nāga, and holding his own tail.
To him, food filled with ghee and incense of resinous juice should be offered:

*Oṃ, homage to the one resembling the color of smoke, the banner of light, svāhā!* At the eastern gate of the maṇḍala is the Blessed Buddha; at the southern gate is Vajrapāṇi; at the western gate is Lokanātha; and at the northern gate is Mañjuśrī Kumāra.

In the northeast corner are all the planets; in the southeast corner are all the zodiac signs and lunar mansions; in the southwest corner are all calamities; and in the northwest corner is the Bhaṭṭārikā Mahāvidyā.

She is white, blue, and red in her three faces; with two hands she performs the gesture of exposition (*vyākhyānamudrā*); she holds a jewel parasol in her right hand and a noose and a spear in her left; she wears a jewel crown and sits in the vajra-paryaṅka posture upon a moon seat.
She has the appearance of a sixteen-year-old and is adorned with all ornaments.

At the outer eastern gate, there is curd-rice for Dhṛtarāṣṭra; at the south, curd-and-māṣa-rice for Virūḍhaka; at the west, milk-rice for Virūpākṣa; and at the north, curd-and-māṣa-rice topped with vermilion for Kubera. Worship with flowers and other offerings should be performed according to this sequential order.
A lamp should be offered to each [deity] individually.
Having filled a conch shell with ghee and honey and having cast five jewels into it, the *argha* offering should be presented.
A face-cloth should be given to all of them.
Thus are the colors, arms, seats, mudrās, and emblems.
Oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ sarvāśāparipūrakebhyaḥ sarvathā bhaktine svāhā.
One should recite the mantra of the Three Jewels in this way for each [deity] seven times, and the mantra for each [individual deity] eight hundred times.
When thus worshipped, all the planets of various forms bestow abundant enjoyments and even produce good fortune.
O Vajrapāṇi, these heart-mantras of the nine planets are perfected through mere recitation; likewise, according to the sequence of their divisions, one should prepare a fragrant maṇḍala.

Having prepared twelve finger-breadths [of space] in the center, they should be worshipped with offerings of food made of copper, clay, silver, and so forth; having offered the *argha*, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times for each [deity].
Afterwards, O Vajrapāṇi, the mantra-words of the *dhāraṇī* named *Gṛhamātṛkā* should be recited seven times.
Then those [deities], beginning with the Ādityas, will provide protection, defense, and guardianship;
they will liberate one from poverty and suffering, and shall extend the lifespan of those whose life has come to an end.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, whatever monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen, or whatever other beings, into whose ear-cavities this sound shall fall, for them there shall be no untimely death.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall worship the planetary deities in the center of the maṇḍala and recite [this mantra] seven times day after day,
all those planetary deities will completely fulfill every single aspiration of that Dharma-preacher.
They shall also destroy the poverty of that family.
Then, indeed, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, spoke again these mantra-words of the dhāraṇī called Gṛhamātṛkā: Oṃ! Homage to the Triple Gem!
Oṃ, homage to the Buddha!
Oṃ, homage to the Dharma!
Oṃ, homage to the Saṅgha!
Oṃ, homage to the Holder of the Vajra!
Oṃ, homage to the Holder of the Lotus!
Oṃ, homage to the Youthful One!
Oṃ, homage to all the planetary deities who fulfill all hopes!
Oṃ, homage to the lunar mansions! Oṃ, homage to the twelve zodiac signs!
Oṃ, homage to all calamities! It is as follows:

Oṃ buddhe buddhe, śuddhe śuddhe, vajre vajre, padme padme, sara sara, prasara prasara, smara smara, krīḍa krīḍa, krīḍaya krīḍaya, mara mara, māraya māraya, mardaya mardaya, stambha stambha, stambhaya stambhaya, ghaṭa ghaṭa, ghāṭaya ghāṭaya—for me and for all sentient beings!

And cut, cut! Pierce, pierce! Destroy all obstacles! Accomplish the task for me and my retinue, as well as for all sentient beings! Ward off all afflictions caused by the constellations and planets for me and all sentient beings! O Blessed One, bestow glory! O Great Illusion, grant success! Destroy all malevolent ones! Destroy all evils!
Protect me, together with my retinue and all sentient beings! Vajre vajre! Caṇḍe caṇḍe! Caṇḍini caṇḍini! Nuru nuru! Musu musu!

Mumu mumu! Muñca muñca! Havā have! Ugre ugratare! Fulfill the heart’s desire of mine, of my entire retinue, and of all sentient beings, O Blessed One, empowered by the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas! Svāhā!
Oṃ svāhā / Hūṃ svāhā / Hrīḥ svāhā /
Dhūḥ svāhā!
Dhīḥ svāhā!
Oṃ, to Āditya, svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to Soma! Oṃ, svāhā to the Son of the Earth! Oṃ, svāhā to Budha!
Oṃ, svāhā to Bṛhaspati! Oṃ, svāhā to Śukra!
Oṃ, svāhā to Śanaiścara!
Oṃ rāhave svāhā / Oṃ ketave svāhā / Oṃ buddhāya svāhā /
Oṃ vajrapāṇaye svāhā / Oṃ padmadharāya svāhā / Oṃ kumārāya svāhā /
Oṃ, svāhā to all planetary spirits! Oṃ, svāhā to all constellations!
Svāhā to all calamities!
Oṃ, svāhā to the twelve zodiac signs!
Oṃ, sarvavidye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Vajrapāṇi, these mantra-words of the *dhāraṇī* named *Grahamātṛkā* bring about all accomplishments.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, these mantra-words of the dhāraṇī called the *Grahamātṛkā* should be recited seven times every day, beginning from the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārtika, after one has observed the *upoṣadha* fast and worshipped the planets and constellations in their midst until the fourteenth day.
Then, on the full moon day, one should have [the text] recited for a full day and night;
for him, there will be no fear of death for ninety-nine years,
nor will there be any fear of the calamities caused by falling meteors, planets, or constellations.
"In every birth he shall remember his former lives;
all the grahas shall grant him their desired boon.
Then all those grahas, having said, "Excellent, Blessed One," bowed down and vanished.

The Blessed One said this, and the monks, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and the entire assembly— including the world of gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas— rejoiced and praised what the Blessed One had spoken. Thus ends the *Āryagrahamātṛkā-nāma-dhāraṇī*.
